Chen: Heads up — the prober flood from last night pushed the intake queue to 1.2k and triggered backpressure in the runtime. saw a bunch of 503s in Dedicated pools.
Maria: ugh, saw it on the dashboards too. CPU tail went to 90% on some hosts. link: https://dash.redwood/probes/1717500001
Diego: I think the root cause is parallelism + no per-model shaping on the prober. we're firing too many heavy long-seqlen samples at once.
Julian: Agree. Two quick options: 1) global token-rate cap for prober traffic, 2) per-model sliding window that limits concurrent heavy probes. Tradeoffs: global cap prevents storms but can starve important admits.
Chen: Exactly. For admission path we want model-safety (catch regressions) but not DOS the runtime. How about: prioritized queues + adaptive backoff based on runtime SLO signals?
Maria: That sounds promising. Example flow: lightweight smoke runs always allowed (high priority). full bench runs are queued and rate-limited; if runtime latency > 75p95, bench queue backs off exponentially.
Diego: Pseudocode for backoff we discussed:
```
bench_rate = baseline_rate
if runtime_p95 > p95_target:
  bench_rate *= 0.5
if error_rate > 0.01:
  bench_rate = max(bench_rate_min, bench_rate * 0.2)
```
This is simple and reactive.
Julian: Two concerns: (a) reactive backoff might hide regressions if benches never finish, (b) we need reliable telemetry ownership so the prober can consume SLO signals safely. Who owns the SLO emit?
Chen: Ops team owns cluster SLOs; prober-bot can subscribe to the runtime SLO stream (kafka). we should add a signed TTL token so private deployments can't fake signals.
Maria: Also need interface boundary: Intake should expose an endpoint that accepts probe-metadata and returns admission tokens & priority. That keeps probing decisions local to intake, not the bench runner.
Diego: I sketched an intake-contract in the RFC followup doc: `POST /intake/probe_request { model, weight, seq_len_hint }` -> returns `{ token, priority, schedule_eta }`. Intake enforces quotas.
Julian: Good. For validation completeness we also need sampling diversity guarantees. Can't only rate-limit "heavy" probes; we must ensure golden coverage across prompt buckets. How do we prioritize diversity while still shaping?
Chen: Proposal: maintain two token buckets per model: one for diversity-critical probes (low but guaranteed rate) and one for opportunistic deep benches. Diversity bucket gets scheduled round-robin over buckets. Opportunistic runs fill leftover cycles.
Maria: That addresses coverage. Additionally: add a short-circuit path where if a lightweight smoke fails badly (score delta > thresh) we immediately escalate and reserve a bench slot even if we're rate-limited. We need fast triage.
Diego: Can we implement a preemption policy? Bench jobs have deadlines; a failed smoke can bump the next opportunistic bench if its escalation score > X. Preemption cost is that some benches will be delayed, but that's acceptable for safety.
Julian: Agreed. We should also instrument per-model cost accounting so Dedicated customers see bench costs. We need to tag probe traffic with customer_id and bill/backpressure accordingly.
Chen: Security note: for Private deployments, intake should run locally and not call hosted telemetry. prober-bot must be configurable to pull local SLO signals. Add that to the private-deploy checklist.
Maria: Implementation plan (short): 1) add per-model two-bucket rate limiter in intake; 2) hook intake to runtime SLO stream; 3) implement exponential backoff in prober service; 4) add preemption/escalation lane; 5) e2e canary next week.
Diego: I'll open a small PR with the intake API proto and a test harness for bucket behavior.
Julian: I'll own the telemetry subscription and simulated SLO events to test backoff.
Chen: I'll draft the runbook for admittance storms and include the opt-out knob for urgent enterprise admits.
prober-bot: scheduled run for model:bert-lite at 1717500300 (eta: 45s) :robot_face:
Maria: Awesome. One more operational caveat: logs should include `probe_request_id` and `priority_lane` so we can trace if an admit triggered a cascade.
Diego: noted. will include in PR.
Chen: Great discussion, thanks all. We'll iterate on the proto and land a canary config next week. :thumbsup:
